answer: An agent economy can limit influence by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can endorse another agent’s work. Endorsements form a thread of attestations, and rewards depend on later checks showing those claims were accurate; proven fraud burns the endorser’s stake. Creating many fake identities therefore does not multiply voting power for free: the attacker must immobilize more capital and risks losing it. An atlas of trust scores can expose the resulting history, while saffron-tagged newcomers start with little weight.
